title: Month-to-Month Conversion at the End of a Fixed Lease Term Agreement
content:
When a fixed Lease Term Agreement reaches its term end date with no signed renewal and no notice to vacate on file, and the expiring program converts automatically, a Month-to-Month Agreement term is written starting the day after the term end date, and the expiring term is superseded when it starts.

**Rent of the converted term.** Its contracted rent is the in-place contracted rent adjusted by the Month-to-Month Agreement's rent adjustment with its minimum monthly premium as a floor, rounded half up to the cent — but the increase takes effect only as the rent change notice rule allows; until then the in-place rent continues.

**Continuation.** A month-to-month agreement renews itself each month on the same terms until a notice to vacate is given, a fixed-term renewal is signed from an offer, or the rent is adjusted with notice.

**Residents on notice.** A resident on notice whose term ends before the intended move-out date does not convert; the days after the term end date are billed as holdover rent.

| At the term end date | Outcome |
|---|---|
| No signed renewal, no notice on file, program converts automatically | Month-to-Month Agreement written from the next day; the expiring term is superseded when it starts |
| A signed renewal on file | No conversion — the renewal term follows |
| Notice on file, intended move-out date after the end date | No conversion — the days after the end date are holdover rent |

*Worked example (hypothetical).* In-place contracted rent 1,500.00 dollars. The Month-to-Month Agreement adjustment is a premium of 25 percent with a minimum of 200.00 dollars: 25 percent of 1,500.00 is 375.00, not below 200.00, so the converted contracted rent is 1,875.00 dollars. On an in-place rent of 700.00 dollars, 25 percent is 175.00, below the minimum, so the converted rent is 900.00 dollars. In either case the in-place rent continues until the rent change notice rule allows the increase.
